summary: Smith characterizes prescribed real conjugate distributions by integer polynomial logarithmic constraints and proves λ_SSS<1.89831, with extreme finite-field point-count applications. This 146-item checkpoint separates existing library carriers, two planned successive-minimum contracts and owner-routed missing declarations; 47 carriers have 141 proposed API statements and 141 discriminating tests. It includes an exact rational numerical certificate and explicit source/version/proof gates. Recursive closure is incomplete.

items.name: Resultant logarithm identity
items.statement: For monic integer P of degree n>0 and nonzero integer Q, L_{μ_P}(Q)=n⁻¹logAbsₑ(Res (P, Q)); it is nonnegative when P, Q have no common root and −∞ otherwise.

items.name: Bounded-degree bounded-root finiteness
items.statement: For N∈N and B≥0, only finitely many monic integer polynomials have degree≤N and all complex roots of absolute value≤B. Consequently distinct irreducible polynomials supported in a fixed compact set have degrees tending to infinity.
proofSteps: Use the elementary-symmetric coefficient bounds |a_(n−k)|≤binom (n, k) B^k; take a finite product of finite integer intervals. Fixed-number-field bounded-integral-element finiteness is not alone this varying-field statement.

items.name: Logarithmic constraint closedness
items.statement: If compactly supported probabilities μ_j on a common compact Σ converge weakly to μ, then L_μ(Q)≥limsup L_{μ_j}(Q) for each nonzero Q; in particular nonnegative constraints pass to limits.
proofSteps: Truncate below at −M, apply bounded-continuous convergence, then take the decreasing infimum; keep the −∞ value.

items.name: Necessary resultant constraints
items.statement: Any weak limit of root distributions of pairwise distinct monic irreducible integer polynomials supported in compact Σ is arithmetic. No capacity or component hypothesis is needed for this direction.
proofSteps: A fixed nonzero Q has finitely many irreducible factors; omit those finitely many P before applying 7 and 9.

items.name: Positive-coefficient separator repair
items.statement: Let the separation in the proof of Theorem 5.11 give F(x)≥λ₀+Σ_{i≤N}a_i log|Q_i(x)| with λ₀=λ_N−1/N and a_i≥0, valid at every x∈Σ that is not a root of any Q_i with a_i=0. For every δ>0 there are λ′≥λ₀−δ and coefficients a′_i>0 for all i≤N such that F(x)≥λ′+Σ_{i≤N}a′_i log|Q_i(x)| for all x∈Σ, with right side −∞ at roots of the Q_i. Hence λ_Smyth(Σ,F)≥λ₀.
proofSteps: Let Z={j≤N : a_j=0}, and for ε>0 put E_ε(x)=εΣ_{j∈Z}log|Q_j(x)|. At a root of some Q_j with j∈Z, E_ε(x)=−∞, so any inequality with E_ε added on the right holds there. Isolated points of Σ need no separate treatment, and 0·(−∞) never occurs.

Compact Σ: E_ε(x)≤εC with C=Σ_{j∈Z}log⁺max_Σ|Q_j|. Take a′_i=a_i for i∉Z, a′_j=ε for j∈Z, and λ′=λ₀−εC. Off the roots of the Q_j (j∈Z) the old inequality holds and the added term is at most εC, so F≥λ′+Σa′_i log|Q_i| on all of Σ. Let ε→0.

Unbounded Σ, using (5.11), F(x)/log|x|→+∞: for t∈(0,1) write F=(1−t)F+tF. Off the roots of the Q_j (j∈Z), (1−t)F≥(1−t)λ₀+Σ(1−t)a_i log|Q_i|. Since log|Q_j(x)|≤deg(Q_j)log(1+|x|)+log‖Q_j‖₁, the growth of F gives R_t with tF(x)≥E_ε(x) for |x|≥R_t and every ε≤1. On the compact set Σ∩[−R_t,R_t], tF(x)−E_ε(x)≥t·min_ΣF−εC_t, where C_t bounds Σ_{j∈Z}log⁺|Q_j| there.

Hence F≥λ′+Σ_{i∉Z}(1−t)a_i log|Q_i|+E_ε on Σ, with λ′=(1−t)λ₀+min(0,t·min_ΣF−εC_t). All coefficients (1−t)a_i and ε are positive. Letting ε→0 and then t→0 gives λ′→λ₀, so λ_Smyth(Σ,F)≥λ₀, as the proof of Theorem 5.11 requires.
items.note: Proof supplied in the continuation of Claude Code (cc-fb70e5, 22 September 2026). It repairs the printed step "the right is −∞", which fails at roots of zero-coefficient Q_i, and the missing positivity of the a_i. The source-level gap is recorded as research/blueprint/errata/PAPER-SMITH-24.json, E5. Uses only (5.11) and upper bounds for log|Q_j|. The positive-auxiliary-coefficient part of G5 is closed for this item; the version gate G7 remains.

routes.title: Partial differential equations, Part II: logarithmic potentials and weighted approximation
routes.reason: PDE LaneC already owns harmonic functions, maximum principles, Green/Perron and Newtonian potentials. Logarithmic energy, capacity, weighted equilibrium and extremal polynomials go beyond that scope. The completed orthogonal-L 2 roadmap supplies the Chebyshev measure, not general compact-set minimax polynomials.
routes.brief: Build on Partial differential equations (tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/PDE), especially LaneC milestones 12–15, and the completed weighted orthogonal L 2 bases (tauceti:Completed/OrthogonalL 2 Bases). Import their harmonic/Green and Chebyshev-measure APIs. Construct extended logarithmic potentials, energy, capacity, equilibrium and domination with the negative-log convention; prove Hölder potential regularity, Remez division, quantile estimates, finite-interval alternation and Totik–Widom bounds. For finite-interval Σ and Hölder probability μ, prove that monic polynomials with roots in Σ and weighted nth norms tending to 1 have root measures tending to μ. Supply the one-sided inversion-arcsine smoothing and sweetening potential bounds, and the exact formulas and rational certificate for Serre’s measure. The arithmetic criterion and integer polynomial construction belong to NumberFieldConjugatesPartII and are imported only at arithmetic consumer nodes; keep the core analytic layer independent of them. Split the inward-smoothing theorem into its analytic construction here and constraint preservation in that consumer. Close G 1, G 4, G 5, G 8 before marking the blueprint closed.

routes.title: Number fields, ramification, Frobenius, and the LMFDB invariants, Part II: prescribed conjugate distributions
routes.reason: The upstream number-field roadmap supplies integer/minimal-polynomial arithmetic and the global/local dictionary, but none of its eight layers plans measure-valued distributions of conjugates or the trace optimization theorem. ArithmeticDynamics DY.4 concerns polarized dynamical small points and PM.2 concerns Weyl/discrepancy, neither this unrestricted prescribed-distribution problem.
routes.brief: Begin after Number fields, ramification, Frobenius, and the LMFDB invariants (tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/NumberFieldArithmetic). Reuse integer polynomials, resultants, Gauss, algebraic integrality and Eisenstein. Import logarithmic potential and weighted approximation from PDELogarithmicPotentialPartII and geometry-of-numbers rounding suppliers from GeometryOfNumbersAndQuadraticArithmetic GN.1/GN.4. The final realization theorem is: for compact Σ⊂R with at most countably many components and capacity>1, a probability μ is a weak limit of root distributions of infinitely many distinct monic irreducible integer polynomials with all roots in Σ iff every nonzero integerQ has∫log|Q|dμ≥0, withlog 0=−∞. Cover nonmonic deflation integrality, bounded squarefree combinations, short integer polynomial families, protected-root coefficient adjustment, Eisenstein rounding, inward Hölder approximation and a degree-increasing diagonal. For closed possibly unbounded Σ and continuous superlogarithmicF, prove optimal auxiliary-polynomial duality and compact attainment, then λ_SSS<1.89831 and the exceptional-polynomial support restriction. Do not claim realization at capacity 1, on arbitrary complex sets, or without the countable-component hypothesis. Preserve and close G 3–G 5 before completeness.

routes.reason: GN.1 explicitly owns successive minima and Minkowski second theorem, including equality conventions. GN.4 owns packing/covering and transference. Route the reusable evaluation-box determinant, lattice-width and crosspolytope flatness suppliers there; keep integer-polynomial arithmetic in NumberFieldConjugatesPartII. Existing covolumes and first Minkowski theorem are imports. BLPS 2.4 supplies the 2 n-vertex polytope estimate; its deep Gaussian/transference prerequisites are G 2.

routes.title: Abelian Schemes And Arithmetic Moduli, Part II: Honda–Tate and extreme point counts
routes.reason: A 3–A 6 supply torsion, Tate modules and Hom/End theory but do not state Honda–Tate classification. WeilConjectures WC.3 supplies Frobenius purity/integrality, not the existence/classification converse. Finite-field classification and extreme point counts extend the abelian direction.
routes.brief: Import Abelian Schemes And Arithmetic Moduli (AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli), especially A 3, A 4, A 6, its existing field-level abelian-variety carrier, and Frobenius purity from WeilConjectures WC.3. Construct Weil q-numbers, Honda–Tate isogeny classification with the local Schur multiplicity, and the point-count norm identity including real endpoints. Import NumberFieldConjugatesPartII realization and optimization, without reconstructing potential theory. For Σ=[−2√q, 2√q] and F=log (q+1−x), prove the lower and upper asymptotic normalized point-count extremaexp λ(Σ, F) andexp (−λ(Σ,−F)). For every sufficiently large square prime power q, obtain infiniteF_q-simple families with#A≥(q+2√q−0.89831)^dim A and separate families with#A≤(q−2√q+2.89831)^dim A. Prove fixed-dimension/isogeny-class finiteness before translating the quantifiers. Ordinary geometric simplicity requires an explicit congruence proof: BCWLPS 5.8 does not itself justify the modulo 4 q claim in Smith 5.14. G 6 is a required acquisition and decomposition task, not an assumed classification axiom.
